department have provided a strong institutional

comprising advanced scientific technologies

Agricultural crops, Horticultural and Plantation

crops, Medicinal plants, crop-specific cultivation

practices, value addition and food processing

methods.

agriculture and improving farmers’ welfare, the

Government of Tamil Nadu is taking earnest

efforts to increase the agricultural production,

enhance farmers income and thereby improving

their livelihood through various schemes of

Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department.

The Agriculture – Farmers Welfare

Department is implementing a plethora of

ingenious schemes based on agricultural

5

restoring the fertility of mother soil given by

nature, distribution of certified seeds that are the

electricity required for agriculture; promoting

high-yielding varieties and hybrids as per the

addition to supply agricultural produce without

wastage and generate income; and food

processing for future use.

7.1. Coastal Aquaculture

Coastal aquaculture in Tamil Nadu has

evolved from a traditional activity into a

commercially important sector. The introduction

of Litopenaeus vannamei (White Leg Shrimp) in

2008 has significantly enhanced shrimp

production owing to its rapid growth, higher

productivity and adaptability to diverse farming

conditions.

During 2025-26, Tamil Nadu produced

41,000 MT of shrimp, accounting for an

important share of the national production of

13.74 lakh MT and ranked 5th among shrimp-

producing States4. The State presently has

2,418 shrimp farms covering 4,609.89 hectares

and 80 registered shrimp hatcheries.

Regulatory guidelines governing white leg

shrimp farming outside the jurisdiction of the

Coastal Aquaculture Authority have been revised

in response to the requirements of farmers.

To support long-term growth, scientific

mapping and assessment of coastal resources

will be undertaken for the creation of dedicated

Aquazones. The proposed study will identify

suitable coastal lands, including Government

poramboke lands and salt lands proposed to be

acquired, for the development of aquaculture

farms, hatcheries, nurseries, feed mills,

processing units and cold-chain infrastructure.

The Department also proposes to adopt the

7.2.1 Seaweed Culture

Seaweeds are a valuable marine

bioresource with high nutritional value and wide

ranging applications in the food, pharmaceutical,

nutraceutical, cosmetic, agricultural and

bio-energy sectors. In Tamil Nadu, seaweed

cultivation has emerged as an important

alternative livelihood activity, particularly for

coastal fisherwomen, while also contributing to

the growth of the blue economy.

Tamil Nadu possesses favourable coastal

conditions for large-scale seaweed cultivation

and has a tradition of seaweed collection

spanning over five decades. The commercial

cultivation of Kappaphycus alvarezii, introduced

supplementary source of income to coastal

communities. At present, nearly 2,000 families

coastal districts of Nagapattinam, Thanjavur,

Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi

and Kanniyakumari. During 2025-26, the State

produced 18,240.45 MT5 of seaweed, retaining

its position as the leading seaweed producing

State in the country. Tamil Nadu is also home to

more than 20 seaweed processing industries,

6.6.3 Maternal Nutrition Kit (MNK)

In alignment with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 2.2, which aims to end all forms of malnutrition by 2030, the Government of Tamil Nadu is committed to improving maternal nutrition and reducing anaemia among pregnant women. Maternal anaemia is a major contributor to adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, and poor neonatal health.

335

Adequate Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation during pregnancy is essential for the prevention and treatment of maternal anaemia. As per NFHS-6 (2023–24), only 64.5% of antenatal mothers who delivered during the five years preceding the survey consumed Iron and Folic Acid tablets for 180 days, highlighting the need to strengthen adherence to IFA supplementation.

To improve maternal nutrition and reduce anaemia, two Maternal Nutrition Kits (MNKs) are provided to eligible pregnant women through Primary Health Centres.

Each kit, procured through the Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation (TNMSC), contains nutritional supplements and essential items, including Mother's Health Mix, Iron supplements, Albendazole tablet, dry dates, Aavin ghee and hygiene support materials.

extracts.text:
1.Preparation and enforcement of land use planning and zoning regulations incorporating infrastructure and

hazard restrictions.

It is proposed that formal land use planning and zoning regulations shall mandatorily incorporate critical parameters such as the availability of trunk infrastructure, including water supply, electricity, and sanitation systems, to ensure that development is aligned with service capabilities. Further, hazard mapping shall form an integral component of planning, identifying areas where development is prohibited due to natural hazards. In addition, hazard maps_ shall specify minimum separation between residential zones and hazardous occupancies. Accordingly, it is proposed to mandate the preparation and enforcement of land use plans and zoning regulations incorporating mandatory infrastructure requirements

and hazard-based restrictions.

2.Hazard maps shall be formally approved and published with prohibited zones, separation distances, no

construction areas

Further, hazard maps identifying prohibited zones, minimum separation distances, and no-construction areas shall be prepared, duly approved by the competent authority, and published for public access to ensure transparency and

awareness and implementation.

-3-

3.Establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on availability of trunk infrastructure

There is a need to establishing a regulatory framework that defines zoning parameters based on the availability and adequacy of trunk infrastructure. This framework shall ensure that development permissions are granted only where infrastructure systems are sufficient or planned to meet the projected demand, thereby preventing overburdening of services and ensuring orderly growth.

4. The above proposed measures are expected to result in a scientifically robust and legally enforceable planning system that promotes sustainable development, enhances public safety, protects natural resources, and ensures efficient utilization of infrastructure. It will also improve transparency, strengthen governance, and support informed decision-making.

5. In view of the above, the Commissioner of Town and Country Planning has requested the Government. issue necessary orders mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving -and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and no-construction areas, and establishing a- regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

6. After careful consideration, the Government hereby, accept the request of Commissioner of Town and Country Planning and issue orders for mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and. no-construction areas, and establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.
